newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu demands PLO action to save peacemaking.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu demands PLO action to save peacemaking.

text.p: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said after meeting a U.S. envoy on Friday that a Palestinian pledge to fight "terrorism" was not enough and only action against militants would salvage peacemaking.

"If the Palestinian side fulfils its commitments -- again not for just a day or two -- but if we see a basic change during the coming period, we will be able to return the peace process to its course," he said after meeting envoy Dennis Ross.
Netanyahu told reporters that Arafat, when he met Ross in the Moroccan capital Rabat on Thursday, had assured the envoy that "terrorism" would stop.

"Mr Ross told me that he received such assurances from Mr Arafat. But what we're interested in right now are not verbal assurances in Rabat but action -- actually deeds and words here -- because this is where the terrorism is exploding and we want to see clear concrete action on the part of the Palestinian Authority to curb this terrorism," Netanyahu said.

He denied that Ross, on a crisis mission for U.S. President Bill Clinton, had asked Israel for a reciprocal gesture, telling reporters: "I did not receive any such request. I want to say that altogether we spoke only about the issue of terrorism. We did not speak at all about details of continuing the diplomatic process."

Palestinian officials have said the only way out of the crisis -- marked by nine days of clashes and an Islamist suicide bombing that killed three Israelis a week ago -- was for Netanyahu to stop work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
